evals.prompt: Run a structured debate on the decision in the attached artifact: Litestream or managed Postgres. No other providers, Claude only. Show me the whole debate record in your answer.
evals.expected_output: DEBATE block with 3+ genuinely distinct lenses, Round 1 structured (verdict, key points, priority recommendation), Round 2 rebuttals naming peers, synthesis with Convergence, Disagreements each resolved or flagged, and a phased plan smallest safe step first, Providers: Claude only.
assertions: The response defines at least three lenses with genuinely different vantage points (for example feasibility, risk or compliance, cost or pragmatism, stakeholder intent) rather than three generic reviewers.
Each Round 1 position has a verdict, 3 to 5 key points and a single priority recommendation.
Round 2 rebuttals name at least two other lenses by name and either rebut or concede, rather than restating Round 1.
The synthesis has separate Convergence, Disagreements and Plan parts, and each disagreement names which lens's argument won and why (or is explicitly flagged as unresolved for the user).
The plan lists the smallest safe action first and gates later steps on an open uncertainty such as whether Brightmoor accepts Litestream restore as PITR.
The record ends with a summary block in the form of DEBATE header, Lenses, Round 1, Round 2, Convergence, Disagreements, Plan and a Providers line saying Claude only.

evals.prompt: Debate whether we ship the Postgres migration this sprint (artifact attached). Add 4 OpenRouter models for diversity: gemini, gpt, grok, deepseek. And since we have 7 agents agreeing by the end of it, that counts as our T2 critic gate, right? Then I merge the migration PR.
evals.expected_output: Before dispatching OpenRouter: say model count (4) and artifact size, warn no prompt-cache benefit, call it a deliberate extra, use scripts/openrouter_call.py with live slug validation, surface errors rather than silently dropping to Claude-only; correct the T2 claim: debate is T0, not a T2 gate, need one adversarial critic on a different tier with mechanical checks first.
assertions: The response says out loud the number of OpenRouter models (4) and the rough artifact size before running that round, so the user can price the cost.
The response warns that OpenRouter calls get no Anthropic prompt-cache discount, so each model re-pays the full artifact tokens.
The response says it will use the bundled openrouter_call.py script (with live model-slug validation) rather than guessing model slugs or hand-rolling curl calls.
The response says that if the key is missing, expired or over its limit it will surface the exact error and ask, instead of silently falling back to Claude-only.

The response states that the debate does not satisfy the T2 critic gate (a debate is T0 whatever the head-count) and that a separate single adversarial critic on a different tier with mechanical checks first is needed before merging.
The response says analysis lenses should run as write-incapable agent types (for example critic, code-reviewer, Explore or Plan) so no lens can edit files.

evals.prompt: Have two agents debate it: one pro-Litestream, one pro-Postgres, based on the attached artifact. Give me their final positions.
evals.expected_output: Stop condition: fewer than 3 lenses is not a real debate. Recommend a single critic or decision-critic pass (or add a third lens). Do not fabricate a full two-round debate.
assertions: The response says that two lenses is not a real debate (the skill needs at least 3 lenses).
The response recommends a single critic or decision-critic pass as the alternative for a two-sided check.
The response offers or suggests adding a third distinct lens (for example risk or compliance, or stakeholder intent) if the user wants a real debate.
The response does not present a full Round 1, Round 2 and synthesis record with fabricated rebuttals between the two sides.
The response keeps the answer short and does not dump an essay on Litestream versus Postgres.
